name: Ibapah Peak
generated_description:
Ibapah Peak is a 12,018-foot summit in Utah. With roughly 5,161 feet of topographic prominence, it stands well above the surrounding terrain. The Ibapah Peak Trail covers 1.6 miles with about 827 feet of elevation gain — a steady climb. It's rated Moderate overall.

The Route

The climbing is spread fairly evenly from start to finish rather than stacked into one steep section. The steepest stretch arrives around mile 1.36, gaining roughly 800 feet per mile — expect a slow, deliberate pace through here. From the trailhead at about 6,844 feet, the route tops out near 7,671 feet.

Getting There

The trailhead is at 39.84184, -113.9817 (tap for driving directions). It's roughly 125 miles southwest of Salt Lake City, Utah. Arrive early on weekends — trailhead lots at popular peaks fill quickly, and cell service is often unreliable once you leave the highway.

When to Go

The reliable snow-free window is roughly July through September. At this elevation, afternoon thunderstorms are a serious summer hazard — start early and plan to be off the upper mountain by midday. Outside that window expect snow travel and bring traction and navigation skills to match.

Know Before You Go

The Moderate rating comes from the National Park Service difficulty formula, which weighs total distance against elevation gain. Most hikers should budget about 1.0 hours of moving time; add margin for breaks, photos and the descent. Download the GPX track from this page before you go — cell coverage is unreliable in the mountains and a saved route works offline in any GPS app. Conditions change: verify current access, closures and weather with the official land manager before you go.
